chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Nasr, from Dawood ibn Sirhan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) saying:

Four (matters) the Believer would not be devoid of, or (at least) one of these: a Believer who envies him — and it is the most difficult of these upon him — and a hypocrite who removes his traces, or an enemy who fights against him, or a Satan who tempts him.

key_terms.أَشَدُّهُنَّ: the most severe/difficult of them — designating envy from within the believing community as the weightiest of the four trials
key_terms.عَدُوٌّ: an enemy — an open adversary who openly combats and opposes the Believer
key_terms.مُنَافِقٌ: a hypocrite — one who outwardly displays faith while inwardly harboring enmity and treachery
key_terms.يَحْسُدُهُ: envies him — a fellow believer bearing malicious envy toward the Believer's blessings or status
key_terms.يَقْفُو أَثَرَهُ: follows/erases his traces — the hypocrite covertly tracks, monitors, or works to obliterate the Believer's reputation and legacy
key_terms.يُجَاهِدُهُ: strives/fights against him — wages sustained, active opposition against the Believer
key_terms.يُغْوِيهِ: tempts/leads him astray — Satan's effort to seduce and misguide the Believer away from the right path

ai.seo_question: What are the four inevitable trials that every believer will face according to Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) declares that every believer is inevitably beset by at least one of four adversaries: a fellow believer's envy (singled out as the gravest burden), a hypocrite covertly working to erase his standing, an open enemy waging active opposition, or Satan striving to lead him astray. The hadith frames these trials as an inescapable reality of the believing life, situating it within the broader theme of patience under affliction. By enumerating both internal-community and external threats, the Imam counsels the believer to remain steadfast regardless of the source of his hardship.
